findings.checklist_item: Extend AC14 (and its test) so ANY failure to resolve last-known-green — API error, timeout, rate-limit, malformed response, not just empty history — degrades to the placeholder recipe and exits 0.
evidence: AC14: 'When the Actions API returns no earlier successful run, the report emits a recipe with a placeholder lower bound... and the report step still exits 0'
AC11: 'The last-known-green main SHA is resolved... via the Actions API' — the error path (non-empty non-success, network/rate-limit) is unspecified
AC14 rationale: 'a missing lower bound must never turn a green main red' — but only the empty case is covered
findings.finding: AC14 handles only the 'no earlier successful run' (empty-history) case, not an ERROR from the GitHub Actions API call itself (timeout, 4xx/5xx, rate-limit, malformed response). An exception raised while resolving last-known-green in a scheduled run's report step could crash the report and mark a healthy main red — exactly the failure the plan sets out to prevent.
scenarios: The Actions API rate-limits or returns 5xx during a scheduled run; the report step raises and the run goes red on a healthy main
Malformed/partial API response causes an unhandled parse error in main_health_report.py
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC14 to 'When the Actions API returns no earlier successful run OR the lookup fails for any reason (timeout, non-2xx, rate-limit, parse error), the report emits the placeholder-lower-bound recipe and exits 0', and add a test_main_health_report.py case that stubs an API exception and asserts exit 0 + degraded message.

Onboarding maintainer cannot find the reasoning behind the scheduled-only model

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC15's new `main-health-report` job with the existing `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` gate: add the new job to that script's `EXCLUDED_JOBS` (with a justification, e.g. 'reporting-only, runs `if: always()`, casts no gate') and add the script + its test to the touched-files list, so `make lint` (AC22) stays green without editing the untouchable `gerrit-verify.yaml`.
evidence: check_verify_gate_parity.py:82-85 `gating_job_names` returns `{name for name in jobs if name not in excluded}` — enumerates ALL job keys regardless of any `if:` condition, so an `if: always()` job counts.
check_verify_gate_parity.py:63-72 `EXCLUDED_JOBS = frozenset({'external','eval-live'})` — the ONLY test.yml jobs allowed to be absent from vote.needs; `main-health-report` is not present.
check_verify_gate_parity.py:44-49 SOURCE_WORKFLOWS includes 'test.yml'; :116-127 evaluate() prints '::error::' and returns 1 when vote.needs is not a superset.
_build-and-test.yml:130 `python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` runs on every leg that calls the reusable, i.e. test.yml's build-and-test job and the Verified gate.
AC15: 'the report therefore lives in a caller-level `main-health-report` job with `if: always()` that `needs` every gating job.'
AC19 requires gerrit-verify.yaml byte-identical, foreclosing the alternative fix of adding main-health-report to vote.needs.
The plan's 'Files this touches' and all 22 ACs never mention scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py or EXCLUDED_JOBS.
findings.finding: AC22's claim that `make lint`/`make check` stay green rests on an unstated premise refuted by an existing gating guard: `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` (run inside `_build-and-test.yml`, which `test.yml`'s build-and-test job invokes on every CI leg) requires `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `vote.needs` to be a superset of every job key in `test.yml` except the hard-coded `EXCLUDED_JOBS = {external, eval-live}`. AC15's new caller-level `main-health-report` job in `test.yml` is not excluded and (since `gating_job_names` ignores `if:`) will be flagged as MISSING from `vote.needs`, exiting 1. AC19 forbids editing `gerrit-verify.yaml`, so the only resolution is adding the new job to `EXCLUDED_JOBS` — a file the plan never lists as touched.
scenarios: Author adds the `main-health-report` job to test.yml per AC15, runs `make lint` (AC22 verification), and the verify-gate-parity guard fails the build with '::error::gerrit-verify.yaml vote.needs is NOT a superset ... MISSING: [main-health-report]'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `main-health-report` to `EXCLUDED_JOBS` in scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py with a one-line justification, list that script and tests/unit/test_verify_gate_parity.py among the files this change touches, and add an AC asserting the verify-gate-parity guard still passes after the new job is introduced.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the report degrades when the resolved last-known-green SHA is NOT an ancestor of the current (bad) head (e.g. verify ancestry with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` and fall back to the AC14 placeholder-lower-bound recipe), so the `git bisect start` line is never emitted with a good SHA that git bisect will reject.
evidence: AC11: 'resolved from the workflow's own successful run history ... status=success on the current branch'
AC13: 'a `git bisect start <bad> <last-green>` line with both SHAs filled in'
AC14 handles only 'the Actions API returns no earlier successful run' — the degraded path is keyed on ABSENCE, not on the resolved SHA failing the ancestry precondition git bisect requires
git bisect requires the 'good' commit to be an ancestor of the 'bad' commit; a mirror force-push/rebase or a dispatch pinned elsewhere can violate this even when a successful run exists
findings.finding: AC11's last-known-green resolution + AC13's `git bisect start <bad> <last-green>` recipe assume the resolved good SHA is an ancestor of the bad SHA, but the plan mixes scheduled and dispatched runs into one success history (AC11/AC12 write on both), so a green dispatch can record a SHA that is not an ancestor of a later red run's SHA — `git bisect start` then errors. Only the empty-history case (AC14) is handled, not the not-an-ancestor case.
scenarios: A green `workflow_dispatch` run records SHA X; the mirror is later force-updated/rebased so the next red scheduled run's head is not a descendant of X; the emitted `git bisect start` names a non-ancestor good SHA and bisect aborts.
First responder copy-pastes the AC13 recipe during an incident and it errors instead of bisecting.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an ancestry check to the red-path renderer: after resolving last-known-green, confirm it is an ancestor of the bad head (git merge-base --is-ancestor). If it is not (or history was rewritten), emit the same degraded recipe AC14 uses (placeholder lower bound + explanation) rather than a `git bisect start` that will abort. Extend AC21 to cover this branch.

findings.checklist_item: State the `actions: read` token permission the Actions run-listing API requires and grant it on the new main-health-report job (test.yml currently has only `contents: read`).
evidence: AC11: 'resolved from the workflow's own successful run history via the Actions API (status=success on the current branch)'
test.yml lines 30-31: `permissions:\n  contents: read` — no `actions:` scope
Listing workflow runs (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs or .../workflows/{id}/runs) requires the token's `actions: read` scope; with contents-only the call 403s
AC14 degrades a failed lookup to a placeholder and exits 0 — so a missing scope silently defeats AC11/AC12 on EVERY run rather than failing loudly
findings.finding: AC11's Actions-API read of successful run history is a new-from-CI integration surface, but neither AC11/AC15 nor the Files section states the `actions: read` token permission the run-listing endpoint requires; test.yml currently declares only `permissions: contents: read`.
scenarios: The main-health-report job runs, the API call is denied for lack of `actions: read`, and every run emits the degraded placeholder lower bound — the last-known-green feature never actually works
findings.suggested_fix: Add `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read }` to the main-health-report job (job-scoped, not workflow-scoped) and name it in AC11 as an auth precondition for the run-history lookup.

findings.checklist_item: Name the exact Actions endpoint used (per-workflow GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs?status=success&branch=main) so the resolved good SHA is provably a green run of the SAME lane being bisected.
evidence: AC11: 'resolved from the workflow's own successful run history' vs the described filter 'status=success on the current branch'
Repo-wide /actions/runs would return greens from OTHER workflows on main (e.g. codeql, terraform-drift), whose green does not imply the test.yml lane was green at that SHA
AC13's bisect lower bound is only sound if the good SHA came from a green run of THIS lane (test.yml), i.e. the per-workflow endpoint filtered to this workflow_id
findings.finding: AC11 does not disambiguate which Actions API surface backs 'the workflow's OWN successful run history' — the repo-wide GET /actions/runs vs the per-workflow GET /actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs — though it also names only 'status=success on the current branch' (no workflow scoping).
scenarios: The script queries repo-wide runs, picks a SHA that was green on codeql but never ran/failed on test.yml, and hands `git bisect start <bad> <bogus-good>` a lower bound that isn't actually green for this lane
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the per-workflow-runs endpoint filtered to test.yml's workflow_id, status=success, branch=main, so the lower bound is a green run of this exact lane.
